newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-GOOSEN SURGES TO FIVE-STROKE LEAD IN WET OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GOOSEN SURGES TO FIVE-STROKE LEAD IN WET OPEN.

text.p: South Africa's Retief Goosen surged to a five-stroke lead in the rain-affected French Open on Friday, but some players failed to even start their second round.
Heavy rain stopped play in the early evening with Goosen at 12-under-par, five shots ahead of Sweden's Jarmo Sandelin, who still has six holes to play in the second round.
A group of players were another stroke behind, including in-form Scot Colin Montgomerie, who failed to tee-off in the second round due to the bad weather.
Defending champion Robert Allenby of Australia will play no further part in the tournament, however, after signing for a wrong score.
Allenby, who beat Germany's Bernhard Langer in a playoff for the title last year, signed for a par three at the 11th when he had taken four shots and was subsequently disqualified.
At the end of rain-interrupted first round, completed earlier on Friday, Goosen had completed an eight-under-par 64 for a two-stroke lead over U.S. Open runner-up Montgomerie.
"I saw where Monty had got to before I went out and I know he's the man to beat because he's in such good form," said Goosen.
"I made an important save from eight feet on the first and then the run before the turn got me on a real roll.
"I don't know how this tournament will finish, but I don't think it will be 72 holes now, so I just want to get as far ahead as possible and hope nobody will catch up."
Allenby, who had flown his parents to France for the tournament, was already struggling to make the cut after signing for a five-over-par 77, which should have been 78.
"It was a straight case of miscounting, my fault entirely," said Allenby.

England's bright Ryder Cup prospect Lee Westwood was later cleared of an illegal round by a rules enquiry. Westwood had played-on after a television commentator accidentally stepped on his ball during his first round of 67.
The Englishman said he was unaware his ball had been moved, so tournament director David Garland took no action.
